'''''Alopecurus geniculatus''''' is a species of [[Poaceae|grass]] known by the common name '''water foxtail'''<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=water foxtail (Alopecurus geniculatus) - Species Profile |url=https://nas.er.usgs.gov/queries/factsheet.aspx?SpeciesID=2681 |access-date=2022-06-14 |website=nas.er.usgs.gov}}</ref> or '''marsh foxtail'''.<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref>
It is native to much of [[Eurasia]] and introduced into [[North America]], [[South America]], and [[Australia]]. It grows in moist areas.<ref>Moore, D. M. 1983. Flora de Tierra del Fuego 396 pp. A. Nelson; Missouri Botanical Garden, Oswestry; St. Louis</ref><ref>Soreng, R. J. 2003. Alopecurus. 48: 97–106. In R. J. Soreng, P. M. Peterson, G. Davidse, E. J. Judziewicz, F. O. Zuloaga, T. S. Filgueiras & O. Morrone (eds.) Catalogue of New World Grasses (Poaceae): IV. Subfamily Pooideae, Contributions from the United States National Herbarium. Smithsonian Institution, Washington, D.C.</ref><ref>Böcher, T. W., K. Holmen & K. Jacobsen. 1968. Flora of Greenland (ed. 2) 312 pp.</ref><ref>Bor, N. L. 1960. Grass. Burma, Ceylon, India & Pakistan i–767. Pergamon Press, Oxford</ref>

''Alopecurus geniculatus'' is a [[Perennial plant|perennial]] grass forming bunches of erect stems up to about {{cvt|60|cm}} in height. The leaves are up {{cvt|12|cm}} in length. The pale green to purplish  [[inflorescence]] is a dense [[panicle]] up to {{cvt|6|or|7|cm}} long which blooms in dusty yellow-orange [[stamen|anthers]].<ref>[http://luirig.altervista.org/flora/taxa/index1.php?scientific-name=alopecurus+geniculatus Altervista Flora Italiana, Coda di topo ginocchiata, Vulpin genouillé, capim-cauda-de-raposa-dobrado, kärrkavle, ''Alopecurus geniculatus''] includes photos and European distribution map</ref><ref>[http://bonap.net/MapGallery/County/Alopecurus%20geniculatus.png Biota of North America Program 2014 county distribution map]</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=Dogan, M. |year=1999|title= A concise taxonomic revision of the genus ''Alopecurus'' L. (Gramineae)|journal= Türk Botanik Dergisi |volume=23|issue=4|pages= 245–262}}</ref> reproduces sexually by seeds and can reproduce vegetatively by rooting at stem nodes.<ref name=":0" />

In Europe, it can be affected by a fungus, known as 'Foxtail Smut', ''[[Urocystis alopecuri]]''.<ref>{{cite web |title=''Urocystis alopecuri'' – Plant Parasites of Europe |url=https://bladmineerders.nl/parasites/fungi/dikarya/basidiomycota/ustilaginomycotina/ustilaginomycetes/urocystidales/urocystidaceae/urocystis/urocystis-alopecuri/ |website=bladmineerders.nl |access-date=24 September 2023}}</ref>

==Environmental conservation==

''Alopecurus geniculatus'' is a component of [[purple moor grass and rush pastures]]  a type of Biodiversity Action Plan habitat in the UK. It occurs on poorly drained neutral and acidic soils of the lowlands and upland fringe.

== Nonindigenous spread ==
The grass has spread significantly in the United States since it was first introduced.<ref name=":0" />

== Hybrid ==
''Alopecurus geniculatus'' is known to hybridize with other members of the ''Alopecurus'' genus. ''Alopecurus x haussknechtianus'' is a hybrid between ''A. geniculatus'' and ''A. aequalis'', ''Alopecurus x brachystylus'' is a hybrid between ''A. geniculatus'' and ''A. pratensis'', ''Alopecurus x plettkei'' is s hybrid between ''A. geniculatus'' and ''[[Alopecurus bulbosus|A. bulbosus]]'' (Botanical Society of Britain and Ireland 2016).<ref name=":0" />
